author: The Current
description:
Bob Mould describes the similarities between pro wrestling and punk rock
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Bob Mould is a punk-rock and rock icon, and he is also a fan of professional wrestling — an interest that included a couple years as a scriptwriter for World Championship Wrestling back around the turn of the millennium. In an interview with The Current's Zach McCormick, Bob Mould talks about the similarities between the indie wrestling and DIY punk-rock scenes. And as the conversation continues, it's clear that Mould is still a wrestling fan.

author: The Current
description:
Make a visit to the quirky record store KEBS Records in Bovey, Minnesota
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Ninety minutes west of Duluth, in the town of Bovey, Minnesota, one finds KEBS Records. Dubbed “the world's smallest record store,” the 8-by-10-foot business functions as a vinyl-focused record store, hyper-local radio station, and multimedia converter. What KEBS lacks in size and hours of operation, it makes up for in character.

KEBS is open two days every two weeks on Friday, 12 p.m.-5 p.m and Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m. Despite this, the connection between customers and the owner, Tim “Edwards” Verthein, is incomparable. Within minutes of opening, the tiny location is flooded with customers who begin eagerly sifting through the latest finds. One of the store’s biggest highlights of the year is Record Store Day, when it hosts a sidewalk event selling all vinyl for $1 each. The record: One customer walked out with a whopping 255 records
title: Visit KEBS Records in Bovey, Minnesota #recordstore

author: The Current
description:
Watch Lucinda Williams perform "The World's Gone Wrong" for The Current's MicroShow series
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Lucinda Williams has a deep connection to the Twin Cities having toured here for many years, and in fact, she married her husband, Tom Overby, onstage at First Avenue in Minneapolis after playing a show there in 2009.

So whenever Williams makes a stop in Minneapolis and St. Paul, even though she’s originally from New Orleans and has been based in Nashville for a long time, it does feel like a homecoming of sorts.

On Friday, March 13, 2026, The Current welcomed Lucinda Williams to the Forum at Minnesota Public Radio to perform a MicroShow, hosted by Zach McCormick and recorded before a live studio audience. The audience comprised MPR members who had entered for a chance to win passes to the event.
